introduction: This file is written by a tool (toolchain/notices in the controller's repository, https://github.com/OmnibusCloud/Controllers), and a build job fails when the committed file is not what the tool writes. No text here is written from memory: each is a file, or a named part of a file, at the address given with it, held to the SHA-256 given with it, or a file that lies beside this one. A text is unchanged but for its line ends.
The controller itself is its authors' work under the MIT licence. This file is about what it carries of others.

about: The engine is built from Rust crates: its own, and those of others it depends on. The list below was made from the engine's own source archive, which holds every crate it is built from (vendor/) and the lock file that names each version. Starting at the C API library with the features it is released with, the tool followed the crates' manifests: a dependency counts when it is of the kind that is linked (not a build script's, not a procedural macro), when it is not optional or a feature that is on asks for it, and when it is for the platform. The walk was made for each of the three platforms: x86-64 Windows, x86-64 Linux and arm64 macOS.

It follows manifests, not the compiler. A crate can be listed of which the linker kept nothing; a listed crate's text can cover files the build did not use. A crate whose package carries no licence text is listed with the licence its manifest states.
